pillar_reactions.evidence: Accepted the premise immediately — 'Yeah, I've felt it. Absolutely' on kettlebells building strength, conditioning and mobility together — then asked two practical questions to work out how it would run in his life: 'Obviously, I would have to buy a set of kettlebells, right? Like, I don't have kettlebells at home' and whether he could drop the gym entirely, 'if I could make it 100% a home workout, that would be better, I think, for me.' The equipment answer was left open ('you just need one', with the weight deferred to the onboarding call), so a cost sitting on top of the price was never quantified.

'Okay. Yeah, yeah, it does' to the what/when/how-much framing, then volunteered that he is already most of the way there — 'I already do a lot of fasting, believe it or not, for spiritual reasons, for physical reasons ... I probably just eat twice a day' — and endorsed the anti-macro position, 'it sucks having to count'. He also volunteered the gap the rep had not asked about: 'The wrong things, but twice a day.' Accepted rather than enthusiastic, because the pillar largely described what he already does.

The one pillar he reached for. Asked whether this was what he had been looking for, he answered in his own words and with force: 'Accountability, yeah. Somebody say, hey, you failed or you suck or why are you not doing this or get up off your , you know?' He had already named accountability unprompted as one of his three requirements at 00:32:49, alongside education and financial skin in the game.

anchors.raw: if it's about, if it's $2,000 or less for the program, go ahead, do it. Anything above that, we have to sit down and talk, because we have to obviously, you know, figure it into the finances
anchors.note: The decisive anchor of the call, and it was pre-agreed with a second decision-maker before the call began. She also holds a category-level view, not a Trevor-specific one: 'not just Trevor's program, but any program, she thinks they shouldn't cost more than two grand.' Any offer above $2,000 requires a renegotiation the rep was never in the room for.

anchors.raw: in my mind, I was honestly telling myself maybe like four grand, three grand, four grand
anchors.note: His own private ceiling sat at $3,000-4,000, which is exactly where the improvised three-month tier landed. Notably his personal expectation is double what he had agreed with his wife.

anchors.raw: I've been following Trevor for a little bit now, actually for a few years now ... at least two years that I've been seeing him online and all that stuff. And I've even done some of the routines myself.
anchors.note: Two years of warm exposure and self-directed use of the free content. He arrived pre-sold on the coach and never once questioned whether the programme works — every objection was about money.

anchors.raw: I would like to cancel the gym membership. Working out at home, where I don't have to travel to a gym, I think would also help.
anchors.note: He volunteered that the programme would replace a recurring cost, and the rep endorsed it ('you don't need gym memberships, anything at all'). The monthly figure was never asked for, so a supportive anchor was left unquantified.

anchors.raw: It said that you can essentially turn your body around completely in about six weeks to eight weeks ... But what's the reality, you know, for a person my age, 45 years old?
anchors.note: The prospect arrived believing a six-to-eight-week timeline from the company's own video and asked whether it was true for someone his age. The rep corrected it downward — 'six weeks is definitely not enough. We're talking about six months' — which supported the six-month price but also put the rep in direct contradiction of the advertising that generated the lead.

unmet_demand.want: An entry point at or below the $2,000 his household has actually approved
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The lowest thing offered was an improvised three-month tier at $4,000, twice his approved budget. Primal University at $200/month — the product this same rep offered to a different prospect the day before — was never mentioned, even after the prospect said 'as much as I want to train with Trevor, if it's not doable, it's just not doable. I just have to accept that.'

unmet_demand.want: A clear total cost for paying in instalments, so he could take a real number to his wife
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep confirmed instalments cost more but would not or could not say how much: 'It depends' / 'if we would split it, that would probably be higher, like if it would be more than two payments.' No rate, schedule or total was ever given, so the prospect left planning around a number that may not exist.

unmet_demand.want: To know whether the programme is safe and appropriate for a knee that is currently giving way
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never addressed. The rep acknowledged the knee needs checking and then described a training approach around it without any statement about what happens if a clinician restricts loading, and without making clearance a condition of starting.

unmet_demand.want: To know what kettlebells to buy and what that will cost before committing
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Deferred to the onboarding call — 'how much it's gonna wait, that also is gonna be discussed with Trevor on your onboarding call' — leaving an unquantified equipment cost stacked on top of a price he cannot yet fund.
